quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?

options.text: Indicate school zones.
Tell drivers to yield.
Indicate construction zones.
Indicate railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell drivers to yield.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. When the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians, you may proceed.

questions.question: When are collisions more likely to happen?

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one vehicle moves faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster than traffic increases your risk of a crash. Driving slower than traffic is also dangerous. It may cause a rear-end collision or force other drivers to swerve.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: If it has been raining several hours.
If it has just begun to rain.
If it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has just begun to rain.
questions.explanation: Pavement is slipperiest when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater and create a slick surface.

questions.question: You are stopped at a stop sign behind other vehicles. If the vehicles ahead pass through and there is no traffic coming, you:

options.text: May proceed through the intersection without stopping again.
Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
May slowly roll past the stop sign.
May follow the vehicle directly ahead of you without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at the stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip stopping just because other vehicles are moving through.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: The amount of food in the stomach
The body weight of an individual
How much time passes between drinks
All three choices

questions.correctAnswerText: All three choices
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating before or while drinking slows alcohol absorption slightly, but it cannot prevent impairment if you drink too much.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on an interstate?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.
You should always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
You should change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes on an interstate. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies. Change lanes as few times as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Use your parking lights.
Use your low beams.
Use your high beams.
It makes no difference which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What should you do if an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you?

options.text: Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.
Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
Signal to the emergency vehicle when it is clear for them to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
questions.explanation: You must give an emergency vehicle a clear path. If it is safe, pull to the side of the road to let them pass.

questions.question: What should you do when entering an interstate highway?

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up and match the traffic already on the interstate. Merge smoothly when it is safe. Do not stop.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after you start down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before you enter curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning can cause you to skid.

questions.question: If you must park where parking is not normally allowed, what should you do?

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from any direction.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from any direction.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for keeping your parked vehicle safe. No matter where you park, make sure other drivers can see your car from any direction.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you approach a railroad crossing with flashing signals, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or the sound of an approaching train.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: When turning, reduce your speed so you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and handle unexpected situations.

questions.question: When must you use your low beam headlights?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: You cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no vehicle from either direction can cross the center to pass.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must turn right.
No right turns allowed.
Right turns are allowed on a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. Turning right here is illegal.

questions.question: When can you stop or park on the freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before you turn left. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another vehicle hits you from behind.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left turn arrow means the protected turn is ending and you must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road ahead curves left then right.
The road ahead curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will curve right first, then curve left. Slow down to safely navigate the curves.

questions.question: What greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill inclines

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop and the harder your vehicle hits in a crash.

questions.question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press down hard on the accelerator.
Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: Before stopping, check your mirrors to see what traffic is around you. Then release the accelerator, move your foot to the brake, and press steadily for a smooth stop.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must immediately stop and back up.
Driving conditions are difficult.
You should drive faster to get out of the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are difficult.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn that work is being done on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is about to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person crosses the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses the street.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes must always have the right-of-way. Always wait for them to cross.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians, even if they cross against a red light or are crossing carelessly.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles and need a complete lane. They need room to maneuver safely, even if it seems like two vehicles could fit in one lane.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not crowd vehicles to your left and right.

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line, what can you do?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that pavement is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, slow down, avoid sudden braking or turning, and increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a collision.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only when it helps prevent a collision. Do not use your horn just because another driver is moving slowly or is in your way.

questions.question: A large truck's blind spot behind it can extend up to:

options.text: 80 feet.
100 feet.
150 feet.
200 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: 200 feet.
questions.explanation: A large truck's blind spot can extend up to 200 feet behind the truck.

questions.question: You must report an accident if there is damage worth at least:
questions.explanation: Report an accident to police if anyone is injured, killed, or if property damage is $1,000 or more. Also report if damage to government property (like signs or guard rails) is $200 or more.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must yield to you.
You must yield to the pedestrian.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog shows that a pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must always yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should be alert. Slow down and look for other traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are yielding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, yield to the driver on your right. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: At night when another vehicle is coming toward you, your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off, using only parking lights.
On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when another vehicle is coming toward you or when you are following another vehicle. Use low beams for the safety of everyone on the road.

questions.question: A traffic light is green but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter the intersection unless you can get completely across.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection unless you can get completely across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection unless you can drive all the way through before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, when may you proceed?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and verifying it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing down to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and verifying it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop completely before entering any intersection with a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: An oncoming car is to your left. A bicyclist is to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Try to fit between both of them.
Let the car pass first. Then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first. Then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Do not try to pass the bike and avoid the oncoming car at the same time. Wait for the car to pass. Then pass the bike.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it mean on a sign?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
An action is not allowed.
Some drivers must yield to others.
Drive below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means something is forbidden. These signs are white with red and black markings. The red circle and slash over a symbol shows that action is not allowed.

questions.question: What happens when a driver is distracted?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
The driver reacts more slowly to hazards.
The driver usually drives faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver reacts more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving makes you react more slowly to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: A school bus ahead is loading or unloading children. What must you do?

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm out, you must stop. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in before you go. Make sure no children are crossing the road before you drive.

questions.question: You see an animal on the road. What should you do?

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very careful.
questions.explanation: Always be very careful around animals. Pass slowly so you do not scare or startle the animal.

questions.question: Why is it important to leave space between your car and others?

options.text: It prevents other drivers from distracting you.
It gives you time to react to surprises.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: Space around your car gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes. Keep plenty of space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: You are merging onto a crowded freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Use your mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Let traffic on the freeway go first.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Speed up on the ramp to match freeway traffic. Yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging safely.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready for someone or a car to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to see you and yield.
Drive very close to the parked cars to give moving traffic more room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for someone or a car to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance from parked cars. A person may step out without looking. A driver may start driving without seeing you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
A one-way street is starting.
A one-way street is ending.
A divided highway is starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road ahead will become a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider.

questions.question: A police officer stops you and thinks you have been drinking. Can you refuse a breath or blood test?

options.text: No, you cannot refuse.
You can refuse if you have not been drinking.
You can refuse if you think you will fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you cannot refuse.
questions.explanation: Wisconsin law requires you to take a breath or blood test if a police officer asks. You cannot refuse this test.
